name: Italy
sub: Municipal raccolta differenziata following CONAI consortium guidance (Comieco, Corepla, CoReVe), typically door-to-door with plastica e metalli collected together.

banana.w: Fruit peel is food waste and becomes compost or biogas via the umido bin.

eggshell.w: Egg shells are food waste and go in the umido with other kitchen scraps.

coffee.w: Coffee grounds go in the organico; plastic or aluminium capsules usually don't.

bones.w: Italian food-waste collections accept meat and fish bones along with other scraps.

shampoo.w: Empty plastic bottles are packaging and go in the plastic and metal bin.

polybag.w: Thin shopping bags in Italy must be compostable, so they're reused as umido liners; a conventional plastic bag goes in plastica.

chips.w: Corepla confirms crisp packets are plastic packaging even though they look metallic inside.

tube.w: Corepla counts toothpaste tubes as plastic packaging, so squeeze it out and put it in plastica.

carton.w: Cities like Milan and Rome collect drink cartons with paper, but some towns want them with plastic; check locally.

eggtray.w: Moulded pulp egg trays are paper packaging and go in carta e cartone.

box.w: Flatten cardboard boxes and put them in the paper bin; large ones go to the recycling centre.

pizza.w: Comieco says emptied boxes with grease stains go in carta, but many towns ask for soaked parts to go in organico or secco.

newspaper.w: Newspapers and magazines are the classic carta e cartone material.

jar.w: Glass jars go in the green glass bell; lids go in plastica e metalli.

wine.w: Glass bottles go in the vetro bell and are melted into new bottles.

perfume.w: A glass perfume bottle is packaging glass, so it goes in vetro, with the pump removed if possible.

tin.w: Most cities collect tins with plastic, but some put metals in with glass.

window.w: Window glass isn't packaging and melts differently, so take it to the isola ecologica or put small pieces in secco.

drinkglass.w: Drinking glasses and crystal have a different composition from bottle glass, so they go in the indifferenziato.

mirror.w: Mirrors are coated flat glass, so they don't go in vetro; small pieces go in secco, large ones to the recycling centre.

tissue.w: Most Italian cities accept used paper tissues in the umido because they're compostable; a few ask for secco.

diaper.w: Nappies can't be recycled with other materials and go in the residual bin, though some towns collect them separately.

pad.w: Sanitary products are hygiene waste for the indifferenziato bin.

battery.w: Batteries go in the collection boxes found in shops and supermarkets, or at the isola ecologica.

bulb.w: Energy-saving bulbs are RAEE containing mercury; take them to the recycling centre or a shop that sells bulbs.

meds.w: Expired medicines go in the special bins outside pharmacies; the box and leaflet go in carta.

paint.w: Leftover paint is hazardous waste and must go to the isola ecologica.

toy.w: Toys aren't packaging, so Corepla says they don't go in plastica; small ones go in secco, large ones to the recycling centre.
